author: Thordur Arnason
title: The supermodel’s booking terms
summary: Muse Wonder’s API rates match Opus 5.5. Wonder Full has a separate booking: a Muse Code subscription.
paragraphs: Meta’s new supermodels have arrived. Before booking one, check which model the price buys.

Muse Wonder launched on 12 October in preview. Its API costs $4 input and $20 output per million tokens, matching Claude Opus 5.5’s standard token prices. Meta’s provider ID is muse-wonder-1.0; OpenRouter routes it as meta/muse-wonder.

Muse Wonder Full is a separate model available only through Muse Code’s Power Usage or Maximum Usage subscriptions. Raising the API’s reasoning effort does not select Full. Keep Full’s results separate when comparing the model your API bill buys.
calculatorTitle: Price the API model you can book
calculatorGuidance: Compare Muse Wonder’s OpenRouter tape quote with Opus 5.5’s published Standard plan using your actual input and output volumes. Muse Code subscription costs are outside this token comparison.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Haiku 5.5’s price depends on how much context you carry
summary: The 100,000-token boundary changes both input and output rates. Price agent workloads by prompt length, with cached tokens included.
paragraphs: Haiku 5.5’s standard API rate starts at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Above that threshold, the rates rise to $0.50 input and $2.50 output.

Anthropic counts cached reads and cache writes toward a request’s prompt length. Each request is priced individually, so a cache hit can reduce billable cost while the prompt still crosses into the higher tariff.
For long conversations and agent runs, context management changes the tariff as well as the number of billable tokens. A one-million-token context window comes with more than one price band.
calculatorGuidance: Compare with Haiku 4.5 using your actual prompt sizes, cache use and output volumes. Choose Standard or Standard long context for Haiku 5.5 to match your prompt length before estimating savings.
